title: Children in kirtan
hook: learning tabla and harmonium at the gurdwara
tomorrow: Fateh asks when God made the world. what does Simran say?

segments.voice: Yesterday Fateh poured Maya's water, and langar fed everyone in the same row: small hands serve. After langar, he heard drums from the next room.
screen: `SMALL HANDS SERVE.` → `DRUMS FROM THE NEXT ROOM.`

segments.voice: Any parent who has bought a kid a drum knows the sound: loud, cheerful, completely off the beat. In a side room of the gurdwara, the Sunday class is going, a row of children behind small tablas and harmoniums, and a teacher counting time with her hand. Fateh presses his face to the glass. By the time Simran finds him, he's sitting in an empty spot, slapping a tabla as hard as he can. The teacher doesn't stop him. She just starts clapping, slowly, until his hands find her beat.
screen: `A DRUM, OFF THE BEAT.` → `THE SUNDAY KIRTAN CLASS.` → `SHE CLAPS UNTIL HE FINDS IT.`

segments.voice: Kirtan is the singing of Gurbani to music, and the Granth is arranged by raga, so its hymns were made to be sung. Some gurdwaras run classes where children learn tabla, the pair of hand drums, and harmonium, the small keyboard pumped with one hand. Tradition remembers Guru Nanak singing his hymns while his companion Bhai Mardana played the rabab, a stringed instrument; a few of Mardana's own saloks are in the Granth. On ang 1075, Guru Arjan says, in paraphrase, that in this dark age, kirtan is foremost. So the off-beat slapping is the start of something old: a child learning to carry Gurbani on his own breath and hands. And the week behind it fits together. A name from the guru. A first visit, with sweet for everyone. Gentle hands on tangled hair. First letters traced on a palm. Stories at night. A pitcher of water poured for a guest. Each one is a way the community hands a child their faith, one small job at a time.
screen: `KIRTAN: GURBANI, SUNG.` · `TABLA AND HARMONIUM CLASS.` · `NANAK AND MARDANA'S RABAB.` · `ANG 1075: KIRTAN IS FOREMOST.` · then, large: `SMALL VOICES SING.`

segments.voice: Tap a slow, steady beat on your knee with one hand, the way the teacher clapped for Fateh. Keep it even, without speeding up. When it feels settled, let your hand go still and listen to the quiet where the beat was.
Children in kirtan. Kids learning tabla, harmonium and the hymns, so Gurbani can be sung by the next voices.
Small voices sing, and a clap can find the beat for them. A full week, done.
